summary: Heinrich Plütschau (1676–1747) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied theology at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1702 to 1704, where he also held an academic post.

Heinrich Rickert (1863–1936) was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Strasbourg. He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (~1891–1916) and Heidelberg University (~1916–1932).

Heinrich Rückert (1823–1875) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Jena from circa 1845 to 1852 and at the University of Breslau from 1852 to 1875.

Heinrich Schenkl (1859–1919) studied at the University of Vienna from 1877 to 1881. He later held academic posts at the University of Graz from 1888 to 1892 and at the University of Vienna from 1892 to 1917.

Heinrich Schliemann (1822–1890) was a scholar in the field of history and archaeology. He pursued studies at the University of Paris from 1866 to 1868 and at the University of Rostock in approximately 1869.

Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler (1815–1894), a linguist and Indologist, studied at the University of Zurich and Humboldt University of Berlin under scholars including Lachmann and Bopp. He served at the University of Zurich from 1841, becoming Ordinarius for Sanskrit in 1864.

Heinrich Stönner (1872–1931) was an Indologist who studied at Marburg, Berlin, and Halle-Wittenberg under Geldner, Weber, Sieg, and Pischel. He served at the Berlin State Museums (1901) and directed the Indian Department at the Ethnological Museum (1925–1931).

Heinrich Uhle (1842–1925) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Leipzig from circa 1863 to 1868 under Hermann Brockhaus, earning a Dr. phil. He later taught classical languages at the Kreuzschule from 1868 to 1911.

Heinrich Wenzel (1855–1893) was a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. He studied at Jena, Strasbourg, Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, Oxford under Max Müller, and Leipzig under Georg von der Gabelentz, where he briefly held a post in 1887.

Heinrich Zimmer (1851–1910) was an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher who studied at Tübingen, Strasbourg, and Berlin under scholars including Rudolf von Roth. He held academic posts at Greifswald, Berlin, Balliol College, Oxford, Heidelberg, and Columbia University.

Heinrich von Stietencron (1933–2018) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Munich, SOAS, and Heidelberg. He held an assistant post at Heidelberg (1965) and served as chair professor at the University of Tübingen from 1973 to 1998.
Heinrich von Wlislocki (1856–1907) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sámuel Brassai at Franz Joseph University, earning his Ph.D. between 1875 and 1879.

Heinz Bechert (1932–2005) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Munich, Hamburg, and Mainz. After positions at Saarland and Mainz, he served as Chair of Indology at the University of Göttingen from 1965 to 2000.

Heinz Kronasser (1913–1968) was a linguist who studied at the Universities of Vienna and Graz under Paul Kretschmer and Erich Frauwallner. He later held posts at the University of Graz (1952), Vienna (1953–1963), and Würzburg (1963).
Heinz Kucharski (1919–2000) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Hamburg in 1938 and served as the Director of the Indienabteilung at the Grassi Museum.

Heinz Mode (1913–1992) was a scholar of Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied in Berlin, Colombo, Santiniketan, and Basel. He served as professor of Oriental archaeology at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1948 to 1978.

Heinz Zimmermann (1929–1986) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Basel, Zurich, and Freiburg, later serving as an instructor at Zurich (1971–1979) and as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Lausanne from 1977.

Heleen De Jonckheere is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who completed her doctorate at Ghent University (2016–2020). She has held posts at Ghent, the University of Chicago (2021), SOAS (2022), and the University of Toronto Mississauga (2021–2024).

Helen Baroni (born 1959) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Grinnell College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Columbia University under Paul B. Watt, later joining the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa around 1993.

Helen Hardacre (born 1949) is a Japanologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Vanderbilt and the University of Chicago. She held posts at Princeton (1980–1989), Griffith (1990–1992), and Harvard University, where she became a professor in 1992.
